observations.disposition_note: Recorded as Qorvo's claim, not an award.
Start date and Day-7 minute entry together state one fact: the case's procedural stage on the review date (trial under way, no verdict). Splitting them would lose the 'still under way' point.
Procedural posture; the cash effect runs through the dispute model.

One claim: Qorvo's stated damages position at trial (the quantified USD 66.1m and the heads it pursues). The cited paragraph describes these together, and coverage requires stating each head it lists.
A contingent claimed obligation; modelled through the dispute, not as a baseline outflow.

Every element of the proposition (injunction scope, costs, interest, fees, disgorgement, enhanced damages) is quoted verbatim in the two cited passages. The finding only restates Qorvo's requested relief.
One claim: the relief Qorvo requests beyond compensatory damages, as the pretrial order lists it.
These are requested (not awarded) components: fees, costs and interest are potential future cash obligations, and the injunction is a potential operating restriction. None is an existing obligation.
One claim: the composition of Qorvo's expert damages figures (one quantified, the rest redacted). The paragraph lists them together, and coverage requires stating each component.
The closing inference ('went to the jury intact') is not in the text. Re-proposing as narrower findings with the 10-Q summary-judgment passage.

The proposition restates the order's conclusion nearly word for word (granted in part and denied in part; no reasonable basis for compensable UDTPA damages; sufficient basis for injury). It adds no inference, and the claim_interpretation observations confirm the posture.
One ruling with its two-part holding; the two parts cannot be separated without misstating the order.
Narrows the claimed damages; no direct cash effect.
One claim: the borrower's stated position on Qorvo's damages (disputes them, but concedes an eight-figure verdict is possible) and the expected timing of the verdict.
One claim: the set of dispositive and Daubert rulings that shaped what went to trial, all quoted verbatim.
One claim: the borrower's disclosure of the relief sought and the possible range of outcomes.
Contingent relief (damages, royalties, injunction), not an existing obligation. The cash consequence is modelled through the dispute instance.
One claim: the disclosed liquidity consequences of the litigation (adverse result, ongoing expense, settlement terms). All sit in the same risk paragraph and must be stated for coverage.
The 'no near-term receipt' conclusion is marked as an inference (is_inference) from the early-stage posture.
One claim: the Texas case is an early-stage claim by the borrower with no near-term cash.
One claim: the going-concern paragraph's liquidity position and its explicit dependence on the trial outcome. Coverage requires the whole paragraph.
Both clauses describe the same liquidity-requirements paragraph; kept together for coverage.
The existing notes and promissory note are already in the baseline existing loans and are not added again.
One claim: the cost-reduction programme, including the paused construction and its remaining cash need.
One claim: the borrower's external funding sources and the absence of committed financing.

Every figure is quoted verbatim. Calling the goodwill impairment 'non-cash' is the standard accounting nature of a goodwill impairment charge (a write-down of an intangible with no cash payment), not a new factual claim. The CFO separately reports operating cash use of USD 7.8m against a USD 22.6m GAAP operating loss, which is consistent with it.
One claim: the quarter's reported operating result and its components, which coverage requires stating together.
One claim: the operating cash burn trajectory (actual and guided).
One claim: the notes' core economic terms (principal, rate, maturity, payment dates, payment form).
An existing financing that creates existing cash obligations (coupon, principal). It is already in the baseline existing loans and is scheduled once, not added again.
The trigger and its remedy (acceleration) are one contractual mechanism.
One claim: the remaining events of default relevant to cash, from the same Section 7.01/7.02 text.
One mechanism: the delisting trigger, the repurchase right and its timing.
One claim: listing-compliance status (deadline and the latest price against the USD 1.00 threshold).
Not a cash item itself. It sets the listing deadline, and delisting would trigger the notes' event of default (fnd_020) and Fundamental Change repurchase (fnd_021).
One claim: the notes' equity-settlement and make-whole mechanics, all from one 8-K paragraph that coverage requires stating.
One claim: the case's commencement and the claims asserted (original and as amended).

findings.proposition: The jury trial in Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417) began on 6 May 2024 and was still under way on 14 May 2024 (Day 7). No verdict or judgment had been entered by the review date.
findings.target: Qorvo v. Akoustis, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417 — procedural stage

spans.quote: The trial for Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc., DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM commenced on May 6, 2024.
Minute Entry for Day 7 of a Jury Trial held before Judge Jon P McCalla - Jury Trial held on 5/14/2024.

findings.proposition: In its statement of intended proof, Qorvo claims that Akoustis owes USD 66.1m in damages for conspiracy to misappropriate trade secrets, plus punitive damages. At trial it will also seek compensatory, treble, exemplary, reasonable-royalty and unjust-enrichment damages. This is a claimed amount, not an award.
findings.target: Qorvo, Inc.'s damages claim against Akoustis Technologies, Inc., D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: Qorvo is owed damages of $66.1 million for Akoustis’s conspiracy to misappropriate Qorvo’s trade secrets for Akoustis’s benefit. 57. Qorvo is also entitled to punitive damages based upon Akoustis’s civil conspiracy.
At trial, Qorvo intends to present fact and expert testimony to establish its entitlement to compensatory damages, punitive damages, treble damages, exemplary damages, reasonably royalty damages,
and unjust enrichment damages.
Qorvo will not pursue these two counts at trial.

findings.proposition: Beyond damages, Qorvo seeks a permanent injunction, costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys' fees, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains and enhanced damages. The injunction would stop Akoustis from infringing the patents in suit, from false advertising of its BAW filters and from further use of Qorvo's trade secrets.
findings.target: Qorvo, Inc.'s non-damages relief sought against Akoustis Technologies, Inc., D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: In addition to damages, Qorvo seeks permanent injunctive relief, its costs, pre- and post-judgment interest, attorneys’ fees, disgorgement of any ill-gotten gains (including unjust enrichment damages), and all other just and proper relief.

also seeks prejudgment and post -judgment interest and costs, attorneys’ fees, and enhanced damages to the full extent permitted by the law applicable to each of Qorvo’s claims. Qorvo also seeks an injunction preventing Akoustis from further infringing the patents -in-suit, from further falsely advertising the properties of its BAW filters, from further misuse of Qorvo’s trade secrets, and from further use of unfair and deceptive trade practices. Qorvo also seeks punitive damages.

findings.proposition: Qorvo's damages expert, Melissa Bennis, puts trade-secret unjust enrichment under a head-start theory at USD 66.1m. Her separate figures for unfair-competition damages (trade secret, corrective advertising, employee poaching) and for a patent reasonable royalty through 30 June 2024 are redacted in the public record.

findings.proposition: Before trial the court denied Akoustis's motion to exclude Bennis's head-start damages opinion (30 Apr 2024). It also granted Qorvo summary judgment that the asserted claims of the '018 and '755 patents are not invalid (2 May 2024). Qorvo's damages theory and the patents' validity therefore went to the jury intact.
findings.target: Pretrial rulings on damages evidence and patent validity, Qorvo v. Akoustis, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: Defendants' Motion to Exclude Expert Opinions of Melissa Bennis on "head-start" damages (D.I. 456 ) is DENIED.

Plaintiff's Motion for Summary Judgment is GRANTED. Claim 1 and 12 of U.S. Patent No. 7,522,018 are not invalid under 35 U.S.C. §§ 112, 102, or 103; and Claims 9 and 10 of U.S. Patent No. 9,735,755 are not invalid under 35 U.S.C. §§ 112, 102, or 103.

findings.proposition: On 14 May 2024 the court granted in part Akoustis's Rule 50(a) motion. The jury may not award compensable damages under the North Carolina UDTPA claim, though it may still find injury under it.
findings.target: Qorvo's UDTPA (Count V) damages claim against Akoustis, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: Because Plaintiff’s only basis for proving damages to a reasonable certainty is inconsistent with the damages cognizable under the UDTPA, the Defendants’ 50(a) Motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.

findings.proposition: Akoustis disputes liability and damages. Its general counsel said on 13 May 2024 that the experts' damages estimates are very disparate and that, if the jury adopts Qorvo's experts' theories, an eight-figure verdict is possible. He expected the case to go to the jury that week.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc.'s stated position on Qorvo's damages claim, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo. We believe the theories used by our experts are better grounded in the facts and the law. However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
Akoustis’ conduct has not caused Qorvo any legally cognizable damage under the DTSA or North Carolina law

findings.proposition: Per the 10-Q, the court granted Akoustis summary judgment only on Qorvo's false patent marking and RICO claims and denied the rest of its motion. It granted Qorvo's motion on the validity of the '018 and '755 patents and denied both sides' motions to exclude the other's damages expert.
findings.target: Pretrial summary-judgment and Daubert rulings, Qorvo v. Akoustis, D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417

spans.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
On April 30, 2024, the court denied each party’s Motion to Exclude the Expert Witness Testimony of the other party’s damages expert.
On May 2, 2024, the court granted Qorvo’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to the validity of the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent.

findings.proposition: Akoustis's 10-Q says Qorvo seeks an injunction and damages, including punitive and statutory enhanced damages, in an unspecified amount. It says the trial result may include an injunction, significant damages, future royalty payments to Qorvo or restrictions on Akoustis's activities.
findings.target: Possible outcomes of Qorvo v. Akoustis for Akoustis Technologies, Inc., as disclosed in the 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2024

spans.quote: The plaintiff seeks an injunction enjoining the Company from the alleged infringement and damages, including punitive and statutory enhanced damages, in an unspecified amount.

The Company can provide no assurance as to the outcome of such trial, and the result may include judgments against the Company for an injunction, significant damages or other relief, such as future royalty payments to Qorvo or restrictions on certain of the Company’s activities.

findings.proposition: Akoustis discloses that an adverse result in the Qorvo matters would create an urgent need for additional liquidity or lead it to curtail or cease operations and file for bankruptcy protection. The litigation has already caused significant expenses, and any settlement could involve substantial expenses, royalties or licensing fees, or restrictions on its products.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — liquidity consequence of the Qorvo litigation outcome and litigation costs

spans.quote: An adverse result in the matters described above would have a material adverse effect on the Company and its business and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code.
Even if ultimately settled or resolved in the Company’s favor, the matters described above and other possible future actions have resulted in significant expenses

Any out-of-court settlement of the above matters or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.

findings.proposition: Akoustis is plaintiff in a separate patent case against Qorvo in the Eastern District of Texas (2:23-cv-00180), seeking enhanced damages and attorneys' fees. The case is at an early stage: IPR challenges are pending, a motion to add Cornell as co-plaintiff was filed 1 May 2024, and no trial date is disclosed. It gives no near-term receipt.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. v. Qorvo, Inc., E.D. Tex. 2:23-cv-00180 — potential receivable to Akoustis

spans.quote: The complaint alleges Qorvo’s willful infringement of the Cornell patent and seeks remedies including enhanced damages and attorneys’ fees.
On May 1, 2024, the Company filed a motion for leave to amend its complaint to add Cornell University as a co-plaintiff, as well as a motion to compel financial discovery.
We are still early in case procedures.

findings.proposition: At 31 Mar 2024 Akoustis had USD 15.2m of cash and USD 10.3m of working capital. It expects existing cash to fund operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025. An adverse Delaware Trial judgment would shorten that runway and could force it to curtail or cease operations and file for bankruptcy. The 10-Q discloses substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — cash runway and going-concern status at 31 March 2024

spans.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.

findings.proposition: Akoustis's liquidity requirements include interest and principal on its USD 44.0m of convertible notes and its USD 4.0m promissory note. It says that judgments for significant damages at the Delaware Trial would additionally and severely constrain its liquidity.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — debt service requirements and litigation liquidity constraint

spans.quote: (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note.
To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.

findings.proposition: Akoustis has cut expenses to reduce operating cash burn. It estimates that about USD 0.7m of additional cash is needed to complete construction-in-progress assets, construction it has paused.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — cost reductions and paused construction-in-progress cash need

spans.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.

Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.

findings.proposition: Akoustis raised USD 10.4m net in a January 2024 stock offering and is re-activating its ATM program. Apart from USD 48.0m of stock still available under the ATM agreement, it has no commitments or arrangements for more funding, and none is assured.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — external funding sources (January 2024 offering, ATM Sales Agreement)

spans.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program

Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
the Company will need to raise significant additional capital to sustain its business

findings.proposition: For the quarter ended 31 Mar 2024 Akoustis reported USD 7.5m revenue and a USD 22.6m GAAP operating loss. The loss included labor costs of USD 6.7m, a non-cash goodwill impairment of USD 8.1m, depreciation and amortization of USD 3.3m and other operational costs of USD 12m. The non-GAAP operating loss was USD 12.5m and the GAAP net loss per share USD 0.26.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — fiscal Q3 2024 (quarter ended 31 March 2024) results

spans.quote: On a GAAP basis, operating loss was $22.6 million for the March quarter, driven by revenue of $7.5 million, offset by labor costs of $6.7 million, a goodwill impairment charge of $8.1 million, depreciation and amortization of $3.3 million, and other operational costs totaling $12 million. As a result, GAAP net loss per share was $0.26. On a non-GAAP basis, operating loss was $12.5 million, and non-GAAP net loss per share was $0.14.

findings.proposition: Akoustis used USD 7.8m of cash in operating activities in the March 2024 quarter and spent USD 0.3m on capex. For the June 2024 quarter it guides revenue flat to down 5% and a further 30% sequential cut in operating cash burn. It expects operating cash flow breakeven within nine months.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — operating cash burn and June 2024 quarter guidance

spans.quote: CapEx spending for Q3 was $0.3 million, and cash use and operating activities was $7.8 million, representing a 31% reduction over the December quarter as a result of our expense reduction effort. We are guiding the June quarter revenue to be flat to down 5%

all of which we estimate will reduce our operating cash flow burn rate by an additional 30% sequentially in the June quarter. Given the top-line projections, the current timing of the CHIP's ITC refunds, and the full impact of recent cost savings, we expect to be operating cash flow breakeven within the next nine months.

findings.proposition: Akoustis issued USD 44.0m of 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 15 Jun 2027, guaranteed by Akoustis, Inc. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 15 and December 15, in cash and/or freely tradable shares at the company's option.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027: principal and coupon

The Notes bear interest at a rate of 6.0% per year until maturity on June 15, 2027 (the “Maturity Date”).

is payable semi-annually in arrears on June 15 and December 15 of each year, beginning on December 15, 2022. At the Company’s option, interest may be paid in cash and/or freely tradable shares of the Company’s common stock, subject to certain limitations

findings.proposition: Under Section 7.01(i) of the indenture, it is an event of default if final money judgments against Akoustis or a subsidiary aggregating more than USD 10.0m (excluding insured amounts) remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for 60 days, after notice from the trustee or holders of at least 25% in principal. On such a default the trustee or 25% holders may declare all notes due and payable immediately.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027: judgment event of default and acceleration

spans.quote: (i) a final judgment or final judgments for the payment of money are entered by a court or courts of competent jurisdiction against the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and such judgment or judgments remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for a period (during which execution shall not be effectively stayed) of 60 days, provided that the aggregate of all such undischarged judgments exceeds $10.0 million (excluding amounts covered by insurance), after notice to the Company by the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in aggregate Principal Amount of the Notes then outstanding voting as a single class;

If any Event of Default (other than an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01) occurs and is continuing, the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes may declare all the Notes to be due and payable immediately.

findings.proposition: Other events of default under the indenture include: the common stock not being listed on an Eligible Market; a 30-day interest payment default; a principal payment default; and a cross-default on other borrowed money of USD 2.5m or more after notice. A voluntary bankruptcy case, or failing generally to pay debts as they become due, makes all notes due immediately without notice.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027: listing, payment, cross-default and bankruptcy events of default

spans.quote: (b) the Common Stock is not listed on any Eligible Market;
(c) the Company defaults in the payment when due of Interest (whether in cash or shares, as determined by the Company) on the Notes and such default continues for a period of 30 days;

(d) the Company defaults in the payment when due of Principal of or premium, if any, on the Notes when the same becomes due and payable at maturity, upon redemption (including in connection with an offer to purchase) or otherwise;

aggregates $2.5 million or more, in any such case, after notice to the Company by the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in aggregate Principal Amount of the Notes then outstanding voting as a single class;
(v) generally is not paying its debts as they become due;
